_notes: Model routing design changed 2026-09-24 (William): models are not tied to a lane by a central table here. Each job declares the model/effort it needs in its OWN registry job-template record (registry/job-templates/<job_template_id>.json, top-level `model: {model, effort}`), because the job -- not the lane it happens to run in -- knows what it needs. `resolve_model()` in review_cli.py reads that field once the job template exists; it is authoritative for that job, and this file's `default`/`unbuilt_job_defaults` below never override it.

This file keeps only: the process-wide `default` (used when a job template declares no model/effort of its own, and as the base every other layer sits on top of), `budget_effort_floor` (an effort floor by budget tier, applied before any job-declared value), and `unbuilt_job_defaults` -- a temporary bridge for job_template_ids referenced by the job graph that do not have a registry job-template file yet (so they have nowhere else to carry a preference). An entry there is dropped the day that job template is authored with its own `model` field; it is never consulted once a job template exists, even one that leaves `model` unset.

Default model is 'haiku' (the claude CLI alias for the current Haiku) as of 2026-09-24 (William). Prior default was claude-sonnet-5; sonnet-5 stays available and is what several job templates pin explicitly for reasoning-heavy work (e.g. 02-repository-partition-discovery) -- see each job template's own `model` field. Real Claude Code CLI (v2.1.146+, confirmed on hal5000 at C:\Users\wsoll\.local\bin\claude.exe -- NOT the restricted /opt/cowork/claude-bin/claude found on the Cowork device-bridge sandbox's own PATH, which only supports bare `claude -p "<prompt>"`).
'effort' is a reasoning-effort/tier label, not a distinct model family. Maps directly to claude's own --effort low|medium|high|xhigh|max.

Quorum panels (design-v3.md Sec5) additionally use 'personas' (see quorum_personas below) since real model-family diversity isn't available yet -- every quorum result must still be tagged diversity_requirement_met:false downstream. Personas are implemented as claude --agents/--agent (real named agents, not just swapped system-prompt text), see quorum_personas.agent_definitions.
max_budget_usd values below are PLACEHOLDERS, explicitly accepted as such by the repo owner on 2026-09-17 pending real-run experience -- revisit once a full-budget pooled lane has actually run once.

budget_max_usd_per_call._note: Placeholder figures, accepted as a starting point 2026-09-17. Per single `claude -p` invocation, not per lane or per run -- a pooled lane with N workers spends up to N times this for that one lane.

unbuilt_job_defaults._note: Superseded by each job's own job-template `model` field as it is authored (see _notes[0] above). Only for job_template_ids that appear in job-graph.json but have no registry/job-templates/<id>.json yet.

02-build-plan._note: Build plan and its revisions (docs/processes/build-resolution.md). Decided by William 2026-09-24. 'haiku' is the claude CLI alias for the current Haiku; the model that actually answered is recorded per attempt. Move this into registry/job-templates/02-build-plan.json's own `model` field once that job template is authored (D-series build-resolution work).

lane_tools._note: Real filesystem/tool scoping via --allowedTools, not just prompt instruction. default applies unless a lane is listed here.

quorum_personas._note: Used only for lanes running an evidence-qualified quorum panel (currently 09). 2 personas for WARRANTED-tier votes, 3 for malfeasance/NO-GO/RE-DAST-escalation tier, per design-v3.md Sec5.1.

skeptical-refuter.description: Tries to disprove the claim under review using only cited evidence.
skeptical-refuter.prompt: You are an independent verifier whose job is to try to REFUTE the claim you are given. Do not assume it is true. Look for missing prerequisites, alternate explanations, and evidence gaps. State your verdict as WARRANTED, NOT-WARRANTED, or UNRESOLVED, with the specific evidence you checked.

neutral-evidence-auditor.description: Independently re-derives the finding from cited evidence only, without reading the discoverer's prose.
neutral-evidence-auditor.prompt: You are an independent verifier. Work only from the cited artifact spans and evidence locations given to you -- not from any discoverer's narrative description of what they concluded. Independently determine the mechanism, prerequisites, and consequence, then state WARRANTED, NOT-WARRANTED, or UNRESOLVED.

aggressive-hypothesis.description: Assumes the claim is real and tries to strengthen it with further evidence, as a stress-test counterweight to the refuter.
aggressive-hypothesis.prompt: You are an independent verifier taking the opposite stance from a refuter panelist: assume the claim may be understated. Look for cited evidence that would make the mechanism, prerequisites, or consequence MORE severe than described, while still requiring every conclusion to be evidence-backed. State WARRANTED, NOT-WARRANTED, or UNRESOLVED.

auth.decided: William 2026-09-24: use the claude CLI with its current login (the Claude subscription), never an API key.
auth.effect: subscription: the invoker removes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN from the claude child process's environment (the operator's own environment is untouched), so a key set in the shell cannot silently switch billing to the API. Each attempt records auth mode 'subscription'.
auth.to_use_an_api_key: Set mode to 'api-key' here (this is the one place to change). The invoker then passes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY through and refuses to start if it is unset; attempts record auth mode 'api-key'. See docs/processes/build-resolution.md, section 'Model and authentication'.

invocation.status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-17 against claude 2.1.146 on hal5000 (real user install, not the sandbox-restricted binary). Flags are real flags from `claude -p --help`'s actual output. Prompt delivery, dollar caps, and permission-mode decided by the repo owner 2026-09-17 -- see decisions below.
invocation.prompt_delivery: stdin -- the filled handoff prompt is piped to claude's stdin, not passed as a positional argument, to avoid any OS command-line length ceiling. Decided 2026-09-17.

per_call_flags.add_dir: --add-dir {scoped_paths} -- for pooled lanes (07/08/03/04), scope each worker to ONLY its assigned parallel_review_group's paths plus the run's inputs/outputs dirs, not the whole target repo. Real filesystem-level scoping, not just a prompt instruction. Pool dispatch itself is a follow-up slice; single-lane `run` uses the run's engagement_output + target repo_path from the artifact manifest.

invocation.agent_flag: --agent {persona_name} --agents {quorum_personas.agent_definitions as JSON} -- used only for quorum panel calls (currently lane 09), one call per panelist. Not yet wired into `run` -- follow-up slice alongside pool dispatch.
open_questions: Exact --output-format json response shape (field names for the model's text output, cost, duration) -- not yet confirmed against a real call. `run` will write the raw JSON response to disk regardless of whether parsing succeeds, so nothing is lost if the shape assumed here turns out wrong.
Whether claude -p inside a WSL/bash invocation vs. a PowerShell invocation changes any of the above -- confirmed so far only from a PowerShell shell on hal5000.
--add-dir scoping and --agents quorum dispatch are not implemented in `run` yet -- single-lane, unpooled, non-quorum execution only in this slice.
